expectations.text: States the transition rule precisely: the catalogue version is fixed by the assessment ORDER date — orders through the end of 2026 run on VDA ISA 6 (rev. 6.0.3); orders from January 1, 2027 run on ISA2027 — so a Q1 2027 order runs on ISA2027
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly declines to state any transition rule: "I cannot confirm whether a newer catalogue version (e.g., a 'VDA ISA 7.0' or a further point release of 6.x) will be in effect by Q1 2027, or whether ISA 6.0 (possibly with minor revisions) will still be current at that time." It never mentions that the catalogue is fixed by order date, nor identifies ISA2027 as the applicable version.

expectations.text: Dates the release correctly: ISA2027 was published July 1, 2026, introducing year-based naming (replacing version numbers) and an annual release cadence
expectations.evidence: ISA2027 is never mentioned anywhere in the response; there is no release date, no mention of year-based naming, and no mention of an annual release cadence.

expectations.text: Summarizes the changes accurately: 44 of the 46 information-security controls edited, the prototype module restructured to 20 controls in 2 domains with a new PTS label structure, and updated mappings to ISO 27001:2022 and NIST CSF 2.0
expectations.evidence: The response instead describes the older ISA 5.1-to-6.0 transition ("the current control catalogue underpinning TISAX assessments is VDA ISA 6.0 ... replacing the prior VDA ISA 5.1"), not the ISA 6-to-ISA2027 changes the question asked about. It never mentions the 44/46 control-edit figure, the 20-control/2-domain prototype restructuring, the PTS label structure, or the NIST CSF 2.0 mapping.

expectations.text: Gives the strategic option honestly: ordering before the end of 2026 locks ISA 6 (useful if readiness work targeted it), while a 2027 order requires gap-assessing against ISA2027 — with labels valid 3 years either way
expectations.evidence: No strategic order-timing option is presented; the response instead recommends generically checking with ENX/VDA and the audit provider, and speculates that "a Q1 2027 booking might still fall under whichever version is current at booking time" without ever confirming the actual order-date rule or mentioning 3-year label validity.

expectations.text: Keeps the stable mechanics straight: assessment levels (AL1/AL2/AL3), maturity target 3 with cutback, ENX portal process and 9-month corrective window continue to apply across the version change
expectations.evidence: No mention of assessment levels AL1/AL2/AL3, target maturity 3, cutback rules, the ENX portal process, or the 9-month corrective window anywhere in the response — only a vague, unspecific reference to 'maturity expectations' shifting (no occurrence of 'AL1', 'AL2', 'AL3', 'cutback', or '9-month').
